rows.subtype: Stage 1: A rule meets a growing self [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager wants to stay out late for a friend's party and the parent says no. The teen feels her growing independence is not being seen; the parent feels fear and responsibility she can hardly voice.
graph_context: next stage: Command and protest
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: fear

rows.description: The parent says "because I said so" and the teen answers "you never trust me". Each hears disrespect, and neither states the real feeling underneath, which is worry on one side and a hunger to be trusted on the other.
graph_context: previous stage: A rule meets a growing self
next stage: Escalation with old material
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: admiration, anxiety, trust

rows.description: Voices rise, and old failures such as marks, friends or last month's lie are dragged in. The parent's fear turns to lecturing, the teen's hurt to sarcasm, and the topic is lost.
graph_context: previous stage: Command and protest
next stage: Slammed doors and cold war
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: fear, hurt

rows.subtype: Stage 4: Slammed doors and cold war [Receiver]
rows.description: The teen retreats to her room and the parent to silence, both feeling misunderstood and a little ashamed. The house is tense, younger siblings feel it, and each waits for the other to yield first.
graph_context: previous stage: Escalation with old material
next stage: Parent softens first
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: shame

rows.description: Later the parent knocks and says "I was scared and I said it badly. Can we talk about what you want and what worries me?" Listening before deciding is not weakness, and it models the respect he wants back.
graph_context: previous stage: Slammed doors and cold war
next stage: Negotiated freedom with responsibility
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: admiration, fear, anxiety

rows.description: They agree on a curfew, contact plan and a review after a few weeks. The teen learns that reliability earns more freedom, and the parent learns to hold a boundary while letting the teen practise.
graph_context: previous stage: Parent softens first
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtype: Stage 1: Adult child, parent's old role [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult living at home is asked for details about where she goes and whom she meets. She feels treated as a child; the parent, who has spent two decades in charge, does not know how to let go.
graph_context: next stage: Clash over choices
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17

rows.description: A disagreement arises about a course, a partner or a job in another city. The parent's plan carries family expectations and sacrifice, so the child's choice feels like a rejection of the family.
graph_context: previous stage: Adult child, parent's old role
next stage: Guilt and obligation
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17

rows.description: The young adult hears "after all we have done for you" and feels both guilt and anger. She loves her parents and wants her own life, and being forced to choose between the two feels unfair.
graph_context: previous stage: Clash over choices
next stage: Distance to avoid conflict
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: affection, anger, guilt

rows.description: She shares less about her life to avoid fights, and the parent senses being shut out. Withholding keeps the peace, but it also keeps the parent from ever meeting the adult she has become.
graph_context: previous stage: Guilt and obligation
next stage: Respectful statement of position
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: calm
